references.text: Both texts deal with unintentional sin (שְׁגָגָה) and prescribe the procedure for atonement when someone sins without intent against the Lord's command.
Concerns the entire congregation of Israel sinning unintentionally and breaking one of the Lord's commands without knowing it, parallel to the theme in Numbers 15:22.
Deals with a leader who sins unintentionally against the Lord's command, the same theme of inadvertent transgression.
Describes when an ordinary person sins unintentionally against one of the Lord's commands, the same concept of שְׁגָגָה (unconscious sin).
Concerns sin committed in ignorance against the Lord's command, with a requirement for a sin offering for atonement.
The continuation of the text that elaborates on the regulations for unintentional sin and how the congregation is to make atonement for such transgressions.
Deals with doing what is evil in the Lord's sight by breaking his covenant, related to the violation of the commands given through Moses.
Mentions offerings for sins committed in ignorance (ἀγνοημάτων), which connects to the Old Testament concept of unintentional sin.
